content.text:
Yes, JusPrin needs its own Terms and Privacy Policy. OrcaSlicer's won't work because JusPrin runs a service OrcaSlicer doesn't. Obico's current pages don't describe what JusPrin does, and JusPrin's sign-in screen already links to them.

**What the app does today.** "By continuing you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy" on the sign-in screen opens `obico.io/terms.html` and `obico.io/privacy.html`. The links are set in [OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:704-707](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:704), next to a comment saying JusPrin accounts are Obico accounts. I read both pages:

- Both were last updated on 5 April 2022. They cover "thespaghettidetective.com and obico.io" and "the tools we provide you."
- Neither mentions JusPrin, a slicer, AI features, or credits.
- The privacy policy names only Google Analytics, Stripe and Chargebee as third parties.
- Neither page names a legal entity or a jurisdiction.

**Why OrcaSlicer's doesn't fit.** OrcaSlicer is open-source desktop software. It has no accounts, no cloud service and no payments, so there is nothing of its own for JusPrin to inherit. The privacy links still in the upstream code point to Bambu Lab's policy, for Bambu's own features. I haven't checked whether JusPrin ever shows those screens.

**What JusPrin does that the Obico pages don't cover:**

- A person's chat messages, plate pictures and details of their model go to outside AI providers. Each provider would need to be named.
- Printer addresses and access codes are stored for connecting to printers.
- People buy credits, so the terms need rules for credits, refunds and expiry.
- AI suggestions can be wrong. A wrong setting can waste filament or damage a printer, which the 2022 terms' general accuracy disclaimer doesn't address.
- Saved chats need a retention period. My notes say every chat is kept raw, but I haven't confirmed what the shipped app actually stores.

**Decision needed: separate JusPrin documents, or one updated Obico set?** Since accounts are shared, Obico is presumably the company behind both, so this is about how the pages are organised. Pages written only for JusPrin can describe AI and credits clearly without changing what Obico's existing users agreed to. The cost is two sets of documents that must agree on shared things like account data. One updated Obico set means only one thing to maintain, but every Obico user gets a policy-change notice about AI features they don't use. I'd pick separate JusPrin pages that name Obico as the operator and point to Obico's terms for the shared account. Which do you want?

Either way, a lawyer should review the final text. I can write a draft that lists what the app actually collects and where it sends it, but I'm not qualified to say whether the wording is enough legally.

## About this draft

This is a first draft of JusPrin's own Privacy Policy and Terms of Service. No lawyer has reviewed it, and it should not be published until one has.

Today the sign-in screen links to Obico's [Terms](https://www.obico.io/terms.html) and [Privacy Policy](https://www.obico.io/privacy.html), both last updated 5 April 2022. Neither mentions JusPrin, AI chat, 3D model files or credits. These drafts are meant to replace those links for JusPrin users.

The statements about what the app collects come from reading the app's source code (branch `jusprin-newui`, 8 November 2026), not from a legal template. Text in **[brackets]** is a fact still to be filled in; each one is listed under Open questions at the end.

<result>All paths below are relative to `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` (repo root) or `agent-docs/`.

**1. Accounts and sign-in**
- The only sign-in server is `https://jusprinv2.obico.io` (`Agent/ProviderProfile.hpp:71`, `Agent/CloudAccount.hpp:212`). It can be changed through the AppConfig setting `jusprin_server/base_url` (`Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:24,36`) or the env var `JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT` (`Agent/ProviderFactory.cpp:126`).
- Browser sign-in uses OAuth with PKCE, returning to `127.0.0.1:41172`. The token is fetched from `/o/token/` and revoked at `/o/revoke_token/` (`Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:105-127,405`).
- Google sign-in: yes, through the server's `/accounts/google/login/` (`Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:124-126`).
- Email sign-in: by emailed code or password, through `/ent/jusprin/v2/auth/code/request`, `code/confirm` and `login` (`Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:197,224-241`).
- After sign-in the app calls `/jusprin/api/me/` (returns email and `ai_credits`) and the gateway's `/models` (`Agent/CloudAccount.cpp:166,175,351`).
- Stored locally: the token, email and model list go in plain text in AppConfig, section `jusprin_agent`, as `jusprin_api_key`, `jusprin_account` and `jusprin_model_formats` (`Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:26-30,213-222`). The OS keychain is deliberately not used (`Agent/AgentConfiguration.hpp:31-35`).

**2. AI chat**
- Four providers are possible: the JusPrin gateway at `jusprinv2.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/responses` or `/messages`, OpenAI at `api.openai.com`, OpenRouter at `openrouter.ai` (adds `X-Title: JusPrin`), and Anthropic at `api.anthropic.com` (`Agent/ProviderProfile.hpp:71-86`).
- DeepSeek and Google are not providers. DeepSeek is only reachable as a model through OpenRouter (it appears only in a test, `AgentUI/src/components/ModelPickers.test.tsx:13`). Direct Google/Gemini: not found.
- With your own key, requests go straight from the desktop to the provider. With an account, they go to the JusPrin gateway, which forwards them to the provider (`Agent/ProviderProfile.hpp:45-57`). The gateway's own model names (like "slicer-1") map to providers chosen on the server side, which is not in this repo.
- Your own key: yes, for OpenAI, OpenRouter or Anthropic. It is stored in plain text in AppConfig as `<provider>_api_key` (`Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:154-166`).
- A request contains:
  - the typed text and any print-issue details (`Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:291-293`);
  - a project summary: project name, printer/filament/process preset names, plate and object names, selection, plan, and G-code history with export file names and printer names (`Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:38-120,295`);
  - attachments: name and text, plus image and PDF bytes (`Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:296-316`).
- Tool results add plate pictures (`view_render`), project images (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1238-1250`), mesh measurements from `object_analyze` (`Workspace/Workspace.hpp:355-373`) and settings values. Raw mesh files are only sent if image/PDF counts; otherwise not found.
- Extra request fields:
  - Headers to the gateway: `X-JusPrin-Turn`, `X-JusPrin-Request`, and `X-JusPrin-Chat`, a SHA-256 hash of the chat key (`Agent/ProviderAgent.cpp:441-447,719`).
  - OpenAI and OpenRouter get `"store": false`, plus `prompt_cache_key`, which is the unhashed project/conversation ID (`Agent/ResponsesCodec.cpp:120,129-130`).
  - The provider's own web search tool is offered (`Agent/AnthropicCodec.cpp:92`).

**3. Chat history**
- Chats are saved locally in the project state under `<data_dir>/jusprin/projects` (`Shell/ShellController.cpp:383`, `Agent/ProjectPersistence.cpp:200-209`). Chat titles go in `<data_dir>/jusprin/chat-titles.json` (`Agent/AgentWebView.cpp:78`).
- There is a local request log that is on by default with no switch found. It keeps every request body as sent, except picture and file bytes, in `<data_dir>/jusprin/request-log/`, keeping the newest 200 files (`Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:109`, `Agent/ProviderFactory.cpp:80-103`, `Agent/ProviderFactory.hpp:29`). Nothing in the code uploads it.
- Server-side capture: the code itself only says the header exists "so the gateway can keep the chat whole" (`Agent/ProviderProfile.hpp:51`). Commit `f00a6bdcff` says the gateway "keeps each chat's newest request and reply for future fine-tuning" (server repo `tsd-enterprise`). How long the server keeps chats is not in this repo.

**4. Credits and billing**
- Credits and usage are read from the gateway's `/account` endpoint (`Agent/ModelCatalog.cpp:146-150`, `Agent/ModelCatalogFetch.cpp:71`). They are shown in `AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:200-233`.
- "Get more credits" opens `<server>/ent/jusprin/pricing/` in the browser (`Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:176-179`, `Preferences/PreferencesWindow.cpp:236`). There is no in-app purchase.
- Payment provider: not found (no Stripe, Paddle or PayPal).

**5. Printers**
- OctoPrint/Moonraker address and API key are stored in the printer preset as `print_host` and `printhost_apikey` (`Printers/NamedPrinters.cpp:359-360`).
- Bambu access codes are stored in AppConfig `user_access_code` (`src/slic3r/GUI/DeviceManager.cpp:443`).
- Bambu cloud sign-in is inherited from OrcaSlicer (`PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:546`).
- Settings tools never return host addresses or keys to the AI (`Workspace/SettingsSupport.hpp:50-59`).
- However, these do reach the AI provider:
  - The connection-status tool returns printer IP addresses and `print_host` to the model (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:253-268`, `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:572`).
  - The add-printer prompt includes printer serial numbers (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:417`, `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts:201`).
- The access-code form says "Stays on this computer" (`AgentUI/src/components/PrinterPanel.tsx:205`).
- Print reports (only when signed in) send a POST to `<server>/ent/jusprin/v2/print_reports` with: G-code hash, outcome, your text, a photo, and project/plate/printer/material/process names plus print time, grams and layer count (`Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:1287-1299`, `Home/PrintHistory.cpp:194-206`).

**6. Crash reports and telemetry**
- Sentry: not found in code. It is only mentioned in comments and docs (`AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts:36`, `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md:365,392`). Analytics: not found.
- Update check calls `api.github.com/repos/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases`, 10 seconds after launch and then hourly. It is on by default, can be turned off in Preferences ("checkUpdates") or by stealth mode, and sends only the User-Agent `JusPrin/<ver>` (`Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp:20-23,79,93-97`, `Updates/UpdateRecord.cpp:29`, `Preferences/PreferencesSettings.cpp:66`).
- OrcaSlicer's own version check is replaced by JusPrin's (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:5634-5636`), and its profile sync is forced off (`Shell/ShellController.cpp:1979-1986`).
- OrcaSlicer's startup sync, which includes the Bambu plug-in check against `api.bambulab.com`, only runs once OrcaSlicer's setup guide is finished. JusPrin never finishes it (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:939-944`, `src/libslic3r/AppConfig.cpp:87-93`, `Updates/UpdateCheck.cpp:76-78`). One unverified exception: a v1 import might carry that "finished" flag over.
- Bambu telemetry is forced off (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:5229-5235,3522`). The Bambu network plug-in is downloaded only when you connect a Bambu printer (`PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:553`).

**7. Connection report and GitHub issue**
- The connection report is offered after two failed connections. If you say yes, it is only saved to `<data_dir>/jusprin/connection_reports/`; the app says sending "is not built yet" (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:984-1019`, `PrinterSetup/OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:742-753`).
- The GitHub issue feature opens `github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/issues/new` in your browser, pre-filled with an AI-written title and body plus app version and printer model. Serial numbers, IPs and key-like strings are removed first. Nothing is posted until you submit it yourself (`PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:150-185,1024-1070`, `Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp:1668-1677`).

**8. Importing from JusPrin v1 or OrcaSlicer**
- Both imports only copy local files; no network calls were found (`V1Import/V1Import.hpp:3-17`, `Home/OrcaImporter.cpp:115`).
- v1's `jusprin_server` setting is dropped (`V1Import/V1Import.cpp:96-106`). The header comment says the opposite, that v1's sign-in becomes JusPrin 2's (`V1Import/V1Import.hpp:11`).

**9. Existing terms, privacy and consent text**
- Sign-up says "By continuing you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy", linking to `https://www.obico.io/terms.html` and `https://www.obico.io/privacy.html` (`HomeUI/src/components/Onboarding.tsx:288-297`, `Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:704-707`).
- Other disclosures:
  - Your own key: "Billed by your provider, not JusPrin. Stored on this computer only." (`AgentUI/src/components/AgentConnection.tsx:363`)
  - With an account, JusPrin receives your messages, settings and attachments and passes them to the model provider (`AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:338-340`).
  - "Local work never needs an account." (`AgentUI/src/components/Preferences.tsx:298`)
- Consent flag: saving a key or signing in sets `cloud_consent=true`, and the AI is off without it (`Agent/AgentConfiguration.cpp:160,221`, `Agent/ProviderFactory.cpp:147-150`).
- Age requirement: not found. `agent-docs/jusprin/` only lists privacy as a planned Preferences topic (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md:659-689,752`).

**Other**
- External AI tools can connect over a local MCP server on `127.0.0.1` (`Mcp/McpServer.cpp:191`). JusPrin itself sends nothing there; whatever that tool sends to its own provider is outside JusPrin.</result>

## Privacy Policy

JusPrin is a desktop app, and most of what you do in it stays on your computer. Information leaves your computer only when you use the AI assistant, sign in to a JusPrin account, send a print report, or the app checks for updates.

### Who we are

**[Legal name of the company]** ("we", "us") makes JusPrin and runs JusPrin accounts. A JusPrin account is the same account as an Obico account. You can reach us about privacy at **[privacy contact email]**.

### What stays on your computer

- Your projects, 3D models, slicing results and G-code files.
- Your saved AI chats and their titles.
- A log of the last 200 requests the app sent to an AI provider, with pictures and files left out, kept to help diagnose problems. Nothing in the app uploads this log.
- Your printers' network addresses, access codes and print-host API keys.
- Your account sign-in and any AI provider API key you add. These are kept in the app's settings file on your computer, which is not encrypted.
- Imports from OrcaSlicer or JusPrin version 1. These copy files on your computer and send nothing.

### What we receive when you use a JusPrin account

| What | When | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Your email address, and your name if you sign in with Google | When you sign up or sign in | To run your account |
| Your AI chat requests (described below) | Every time you send a message to the AI assistant | To get a reply from our AI provider. We also keep the latest request and reply of each chat to improve future AI models **[see Open questions: opt-out]** |
| How many AI replies you used | Every reply | To count your credits |
| Print reports: a fingerprint of the G-code file, whether the print worked, your note, your photo, the project, plate, printer, material and process names, print time, weight in grams and layer count | Only when you send a report | To show your print history and **[other use, if any]** |
| Payment details | When you buy credits or a plan on our pricing page | Handled by **[payment processor]**. We do not see your full card number |

An AI chat request contains:

- the message you typed, and any pictures, PDFs or text files you attach;
- a summary of the open project: its name, the names of the printer, filament and process profiles, plate and object names, the settings the AI reads or changes, and file names of exported G-code;
- pictures of your build plate that the app draws, and measurements of your models (size, volume, overhangs);
- when you are setting up a printer, the printer's address on your local network and its serial number.

A chat request does not contain your printer access codes, your print-host API keys, or your raw 3D model files.

### Who else receives information

- **AI providers.** With a JusPrin account, we pass your chat requests to **[OpenAI, and any other providers we use]** to produce replies. If you add your own API key for OpenAI, Anthropic or OpenRouter instead, the app sends requests straight from your computer to that provider. We never receive them, and that provider's terms and privacy policy apply.
- **Web search.** The AI may use its provider's web search to answer a question. The search terms are written by the AI from your chat.
- **Payment processor.** **[Name]** processes purchases under its own privacy policy.
- **GitHub.** The app checks GitHub for new versions, sending only the app's version number. You can turn this off in Preferences. If you choose to report a problem as a GitHub issue, the app opens a pre-filled page in your browser with printer serial numbers and addresses removed. Nothing is posted until you submit it, and GitHub issues are public.
- **Printer makers.** If you connect a Bambu Lab printer, the app downloads Bambu Lab's network plug-in. If you sign in to a Bambu Lab account in the app, Bambu Lab's privacy policy covers that sign-in.

We do not sell your personal information or share it for advertising. **[Confirm: the app sends no analytics or crash reports. See Open questions.]**

### How long we keep it

- Account details: until you delete your account.
- Chats kept on our servers: **[retention period]**.
- Print reports: **[retention period]**.
- Payment records: as long as tax and accounting law requires.

### Your choices and rights

- You can slice and print without an account. The AI assistant needs either a JusPrin account or your own API key.
- You can turn off update checks in Preferences.
- You can ask us to show, correct, export or delete your information by writing to **[privacy contact email]**. **[Lawyer: rights under GDPR, UK GDPR and California law, and how to complain to a regulator.]**
- **[If added: how to stop your chats being used to improve AI models.]**

### Children

JusPrin accounts are not meant for children under **[13, or 16 in the EU and UK]**. If you believe a child has given us information, write to us and we will delete it.

### International transfers

We and our AI providers process information in **[countries]**. **[Lawyer: transfer safeguards for users in the EU and UK.]**

### Changes to this policy

We will post changes at **[policy URL]** and tell you in the app or by email before an important change takes effect.

Last updated: **[date]**

from.content:
## Terms of Service

These terms cover JusPrin accounts, the AI assistant, credits and print reports. They don't limit your rights to the JusPrin app under its open-source license.

### 1. Agreeing to these terms

By creating a JusPrin account or using the AI assistant through one, you agree to these terms and to the Privacy Policy. If you use JusPrin for a business, you agree on its behalf. You must be at least **[13, or 16 in the EU and UK]**, and have a parent's permission if you are under the age of majority where you live.

### 2. The app and its license

JusPrin is free, open-source software based on OrcaSlicer, released under the GNU Affero General Public License version 3. That license, not these terms, governs copying, changing and sharing the app's code. These terms apply only to the online services we run: accounts, the AI assistant through a JusPrin account, credits and print reports.

### 3. Your account

Give us accurate information and keep your sign-in to yourself. You are responsible for what happens under your account. Tell us at **[support email]** if you think someone else has used it.

### 4. The AI assistant

The AI assistant suggests and changes slicing settings, arranges objects, connects printers and answers questions. It can be wrong.

- Check what it changed before you print. A wrong setting can waste filament, ruin a print, or damage your printer, for example by heating too hot or moving outside the build area.
- You decide what to print and when. You are responsible for your printer, what it makes, and supervising it while it runs.
- Don't rely on the assistant for safety-critical decisions, such as parts that carry loads, touch food, or go in or on the body.
- Replies come from third-party AI models that we don't control. The assistant may be slow or unavailable, and models may change.

### 5. Credits and plans

- Using the AI assistant through a JusPrin account uses credits. Each reply uses credits based on the model you chose. Chat titles cost nothing.
- You can get credits from **[free monthly credits, a plan, or a one-time purchase]** on our pricing page. Prices and what each plan includes are shown there and may change, with **[notice period]** notice before a change affects a plan you pay for.
- Credits that come with a free account or a plan expire **[when]**. Purchased credits expire **[when, or never]**.
- Credits have no cash value. You can't sell or transfer them, and they are not refunded when they expire or when an account is closed, except as section 9 or the law requires.
- Plans renew automatically until you cancel. **[Cancellation and refund rules, including the 7-day refund in Obico's current terms if it should carry over.]**
- **[If kept: JusPrin version 1 subscribers keep their original price for as long as they stay subscribed.]**

### 6. Your content

Your models, projects, messages, attachments, photos and print reports stay yours. You give us permission to store, process and send them to our AI providers as needed to run the service. **[If kept: and to use chats to improve AI models, as the Privacy Policy describes.]**

Only upload or attach things you have the right to share. AI replies are given to you to use as you like, subject to the law and the providers' rules.

### 7. What you must not do

- Use the service to break the law, including making items that are illegal where you live.
- Get around credit limits, share an account, or resell access to the AI assistant.
- Send automated requests to our servers other than through the app, or try to break into or overload them.
- Use the AI assistant to create content that is abusive, infringing or harmful.

### 8. Other companies' services

Printers, printer firmware, print hosts such as OctoPrint and Moonraker, Bambu Lab's services and AI providers belong to other companies. Their terms apply, and we are not responsible for them.

### 9. Ending your account

You can stop using the service and ask us to delete your account at any time. We may suspend or close an account that breaks these terms, with notice where we reasonably can. **[What happens to unused paid credits.]**

### 10. Disclaimers and limits on liability

**[Lawyer to draft.]** The service is provided "as is". To the extent the law allows, we are not liable for failed prints, wasted material, damage to printers or property, or indirect losses. Our total liability is limited to **[the amount you paid us in the past 12 months, or a fixed sum]**. Nothing here limits rights you have under consumer law that can't be waived.

### 11. Changes to these terms

We will post changes at **[terms URL]** and tell you in the app or by email before an important change takes effect. If you keep using the service after that, you accept the new terms.

### 12. Law and disputes

These terms are governed by the laws of **[state or country]**. **[Lawyer: courts, arbitration, and consumer-law exceptions.]**

### 13. Contact

**[Legal name and postal address]**, **[support email]**.

Last updated: **[date]**

## Open questions

The first four come from comparing the draft with what the app does today. They may need a product decision, not just a fact.

- [ ] **Chats kept for training.** The JusPrin server keeps each chat's latest request and reply "for future fine-tuning" (commit `f00a6bdcff`, 29 October 2026). The app's Preferences text says JusPrin passes chats to the model provider but doesn't mention keeping them. Should users be able to opt out, and should the in-app text say so? Affects Privacy › What we receive, Your choices, and Terms §6.
- [ ] **Analytics and crash reports.** The app sends none today: no Sentry or analytics code was found. The project's guidelines expect errors to reach Sentry. If crash reporting is added, the Privacy Policy must list it first. Affects Privacy › Who else receives information.
- [ ] **Local request log.** The app keeps the last 200 AI requests on disk, on by default and with no setting to turn it off. Is that acceptable, or should Preferences get a switch? Affects Privacy › What stays on your computer.
- [ ] **Sign-ins and keys stored unencrypted.** The account sign-in and AI provider keys are kept in plain text in the settings file; the code deliberately avoids the system keychain. The draft says so plainly. Keep that wording, or change the storage first?
- [ ] Legal name and postal address of the company, and which state or country's law governs. Affects Privacy › Who we are, and Terms §12–13.
- [ ] Privacy and support email addresses.
- [ ] Where the pages will live (for example a JusPrin website or `obico.io/jusprin/...`). Once published, the sign-in screen's two links in `OrcaHomeBackend.cpp` must change to point there.
- [ ] Which AI providers the JusPrin server sends chats to, where they process data, and whether each one keeps or trains on it. Affects Privacy › Who else receives information, and International transfers.
- [ ] How long the server keeps chats and print reports.
- [ ] What print reports are used for beyond print history.
- [ ] Payment processor for credits and plans. Obico's current policy names Stripe and Chargebee.
- [ ] Credit rules: what free accounts and each plan get, when each kind of credit expires, the refund rule, and whether JusPrin version 1 subscribers keep their original price. Affects Terms §5 and §9.
- [ ] Minimum age: 13, or 16 in the EU and UK, or a single age everywhere.
- [ ] Whether Obico's own Privacy Policy and Terms should add a line pointing JusPrin users to these pages.
- [ ] Lawyer: liability limits, disputes, consumer-law exceptions, and EU and UK data-protection wording.

content.text:
I've drafted the [JusPrin Terms and Privacy Policy](https://claude.ai/artifact/3USmxZnqCvQGPC3Bx9rf5V). You can edit it inline or leave comments and I'll revise. No lawyer has reviewed it yet.

The statements about data are based on the app's code, not a legal template. Facts I couldn't find, like the company's legal name, payment processor, retention periods and governing law, are left in brackets. They're also listed as open questions at the end of the document.

Four things the app does today need your call, because the text has to say what the app really does:

- **Chats kept for training.** JusPrin's server keeps each chat's latest request and reply for future fine-tuning, which commit `f00a6bdcff` documents. The app's Preferences text doesn't mention this, and users have no way to opt out.
- **Unencrypted sign-in and keys.** The account sign-in and any AI provider keys sit in plain text in the app's settings file. The draft says so as it is.
- **Local request log.** The app keeps the last 200 AI requests on disk by default, with no setting to turn that off.
- **No crash reports.** The app sends no crash reports or analytics today. If crash reporting through Sentry is added later, the policy has to list it first.

When the pages are published, the two links on the sign-in screen in [OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:706](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Home/OrcaHomeBackend.cpp:706) need to point to them.
